description.narrative:
FN: s utvecklingsprogram (UNDP) har från Sida ansökt om 40 miljoner kronor för att finansiera insatsen Liberia Electoral Support Project (LESP) under 2021 - 2024. Insatsen bedöms vara i linje med de övergripande prioriteringarna och inriktningen för Sveriges Strategi för utvecklingsbistånd i Liberia 2021 - 2025.
Det övergripande målet för detta projekt är att fortsätta stärka valinstitutionerna- och processerna. Som ett övegripande mål bör denna cykel präglas av att ytterligare förstärka det nationellt ägandet och framsteg mot fredliga, trovärdiga, inkluderande och transparenta valprocesser i Liberia.
Den totala budgeten för LESP-projektets varaktighet är 16,180,764.00 miljoner USD. Vid tidpunkten för denna bedömning är det svenska bidraget 40.0 miljoner kronor, cirka 4,8 miljoner USD. UNDP:s planerade stöd från egna resurser är 1.5 miljoner USD. När det gäller andra externa givarresurser har EU visat ett intresse av att finansiera valprojektet med 15.0 miljoner EUR och Irland har uttryckt ett åtagande om 2.0 miljoner EUR.

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has through Sida applied for funding of 40 million SEK to fund the Liberia Electoral Support Project (LESP) during 2021 - 2024. The contribution is assessed to be in line with the overarching priorities and direction of Swedish Strategy for Development cooperation in Liberia 2021 - 2025.
The overall objective of this Project is to continue strengthening the electoral institutions and processes. As an overreaching goal, this cycle should be marked by further enhanced national ownership as well as continued progress towards peaceful, credible, inclusive and transparent electoral processes in Liberia.
The total budget for the LESP project duration is USD 16,180,764.00 million. At the time of this appraisal, the Swedish contribution is SEK 40.0 million, approximately USD 4.8 million. UNDP core contribution is so far at USD 1.5 million. As for other external donor resources, the EU has indicated an interest to fund the elections project with EUR 15.0 million and Ireland has made a commitment of EUR 2.0 million.

Overall goal: The overall goal of this Project is more inclusive, effective, transparent and accountable governance of Liberia. This goal will be achieved through improved legal and regulatory frameworks, stronger public institutions, more engaged and responsible stakeholders, and peaceful electoral and democratic processes. As an overreaching goal, this electoral cycle will also enhance national ownership as well as continued progress towards peaceful, credible, inclusive and transparent electoral processes in Liberia. Expected results: Output 1: Inclusion and transparency of the electoral process is strengthened 1.1 NEC strategic approach to communication, external relations, and disinformation management 1.2 Strengthening capacity of NEC, civil society, and other actors in conducting civic and voter education 1.3 Improved access and opportunity of the right to vote to vulnerable groups Output 2: Institutional capacity and accountability of NEC and electoral stakeholders enhanced 2.1 Project's capacity-building support is based in detailed and realistic assessment at all levels 2.2 Technical Capacity and Skills of NEC at All Levels are strengthened 2.3 Enhanced technical capacity of electoral stakeholders towards greater accountability and electoral integrity 2.4 Increased Integrity and Sustainability of Electoral Operations, including Voter Registration Process 2.5: NEC Infrastructure Strengthening towards Greater Electoral Integrity Output 3: Conflict prevention and mitigation mechanisms to support peaceful conduct of elections are strengthened 3.1 Electoral security further improved 3.2 Awareness raised and mitigation measures implemented to mitigate Violence Against Women in Elections (VAWIE)

description.narrative:
The year of 2023 was a major year for Liberia and for the implementation of the LESP. Being the election year, the project had several achievements before, during and after the election days. Below a summary of some of the results achieved during 2023:
- Strengthened capacity of NEC communication department incl. supporting the negotiating with telecompanies for the free dissemination of SMS, which enhanced public information around elections and helped improve the confidence of the electorate in the process.
- Supported the establishement and training of 81 CVE cells comprised of 243 community-based organizations. The focus on locally-led interventions likely contributed to the high number of registered voters and to the high voter turnout during the General Election and the run-off (78.86% and 66.12%).
- Improved facilitation-skills and ability to conduct quality training independently in the future after 24 key staff of NEC became accredited BRIDGE-facilitators. LESP also supported unity and coherence of the NEC BoC, the Secretariat and other key staff by conducting the BRIDGE Institutional Excellence Module. This contributed to the unity of the commission during the elections.
- Technical assistance to the Data Centre to support the set-up, security and functioning of key applications (voter registration, recruitment portal, candidate nomination application, voter management, results portal etc.). This contributed to increased transparency and integrity of key electoral systems critical for the acceptance of the electoral outcomes by the public.
- In collaboration with Internews, LESP held media training courses and supported the revision of the media code of conduct. The activities supported the improved standards of media coverage, enhanced responsible reporting and to some extent reduced misinformation.
- With LESP support, NEC signed a MoU with the Liberian National Bar Association (LNBA) and organized regional dialogues to strengthen the knowledge of electoral stakeholders in electoral dispute resolution (EDR). LESP also supported the training of lawyers, magistrates, hearing officers and clerks in EDR. All of which contributed to the process of handling the 57 incoming election complaints in a timely manner.
- LESP (together with other UN organisations) supported NEC in the process of revising the Farmington River Declaration with a commitment to uphold peace throughout the electoral process. The declaration was signed by political parties and independent candidates and played an important role in back-channel diplomacy to ensure peaceful conduct by political actors.
- LESP contributed to elevating the issue of VAWIE/P (violence against women in elections/politics) to the national discourse - it was included in the revised Farmington Declaration, awareness was increased and capacities were strengthened in political parties, civil society and government ministries, agencies and commissions. It is likely that this contributed to the low incidences of VAWIE/P during the elections.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
